source_refs.note: Book p. 45-47: 2.8 higher-order derivatives, notation table, Examples 11-14, Challenge! box (y10)

blocks.text: Pichle sections mein humne ek function ka derivative nikalna seekha. Ab ek dilchasp baat dekhiye: derivative \(f'\) khud bhi ek function hai. To kya us ka bhi derivative nikal sakte hain? Bilkul! Isi ko higher-order derivatives (ooncha darja ke derivatives) kehte hain. Achhi khabar yeh hai ke koi naya rule seekhna nahi parega; jo rules aap jaante hain, wohi baar baar lagane hain.

Kitab ki baat: function \(f\) ka derivative \(f'\) khud ek function hai, is liye us ka bhi apna derivative ho sakta hai. Agar \(f'\) differentiable ho to us ke derivative ko \(f''\) likhte hain aur ise \(f\) ka second derivative kehte hain. Jab tak naya function differentiable rahe, hum yeh amal jaari rakh kar teesra, chautha, paanchwan aur is se bhi aage ke derivatives nikal sakte hain. In lagataar derivatives ko higher-order derivatives kehte hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Gaari ki misaal lijiye. Agar \(s(t)\) gaari ki position (jagah) hai, to \(s'(t)\) us ki velocity (raftaar) hai, aur \(s''(t)\), yani velocity ka derivative, acceleration (raftaar kitni tezi se badal rahi hai) hai. Jab aap accelerator dabate hain to raftaar barhti hai: yeh second derivative ka kaam hai.
Isi tarah \(f''(x)\) batata hai ke slope \(f'(x)\) khud kitni tezi se badal raha hai. Aage maxima aur minima wale sabaq mein second derivative bohat kaam aayega.
Higher-order derivatives ke liye aam tor par yeh notations (likhne ke tareeqe) istemal hote hain:

blocks.caption: Commonly used notations for higher-order derivatives (as printed in the book)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Notation ko ghor se parhiye, yahan bohat se bachche phisalte hain:
1. \(y_{1}\), \(y_{2}\), ... derivatives hain (\(y_{1} = \frac{dy}{dx}\)); yeh \(y\) ko 1 ya 2 se multiply karna nahi.
2. \(f^{(4)}(x)\) bracket ke saath chautha derivative hai; bina bracket \(f^{4}(x)\) aam tor par chauthi power samjhi jati hai. Chauthe derivative se aage bohat sare dash lagane ki bajaye bracket mein number likhte hain.
3. \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\) mein upar 2 \(d\) ke saath aur neeche \(x\) ke saath hai. Yeh \(\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^{2}\) nahi, yani slope ka square nahi.
4. \(D\) ka matlab \(\frac{d}{dx}\) hai, to \(D^{2}y = \frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\).

Ab kitab ki chaar misaalein dekhte hain. Pehli polynomial ki hai, jahan derivatives aakhir mein ruk jate hain. Doosri parametric equations ki hai, jahan second derivative nikalne ka sahi tareeqa seekhenge. Teesri exponential function ka pattern sikhati hai, aur chauthi mein logarithm ko pehle simplify kar ke bohat se derivatives nikalte hain. Har misaal mein pehle khud koshish kijiye, phir steps se milaiye.

blocks.title: Example 11
blocks.problem: Find the higher-order derivatives of the function \(f(x) = \frac{1}{4}x^{4} - x^{3} + \frac{1}{2}x^{2} - 3\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = \frac{1}{4}x^{4} - x^{3} + \frac{1}{2}x^{2} - 3\), yeh degree 4 ka polynomial hai.
Maloom karna: \(f'(x), f''(x), f'''(x), \ldots\), yani is ke saare higher-order derivatives.
Tareeqa: har term ko power rule \(\frac{d}{dx}x^{n} = nx^{n-1}\) se differentiate karte jayein. Har dafa degree ek kam hoti hai, is liye paanch dafa ke baad kuch nahi bachega. Yeh sab se aasaan qisam ka sawal hai, is se notation ki practice ho jayegi.

Pehla derivative
\[f'(x) = \dfrac{1}{4}\cdot 4x^{3} - 3x^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot 2x - 0\]
\[= x^{3} - 3x^{2} + x\]
Kyun: har term par power rule lagaya: power aage aati hai aur ek kam ho jati hai. Constant \(-3\) ka derivative 0 hai. Dekhiye \(\frac{1}{4}\) aur 4 cancel ho gaye, aur \(\frac{1}{2}\) aur 2 bhi.

Doosra aur teesra derivative
\[f''(x) = 3x^{2} - 6x + 1\]
\[f'''(x) = 6x - 6\]
Kyun: bas pichli line ko dobara differentiate kiya. \(x\) ka derivative 1 aur constant ka 0 hota hai.

Chautha, paanchwan aur aage ke derivatives
\[f^{(4)}(x) = 6\]
\[f^{(5)}(x) = 0\]
\[f^{(n)}(x) = 0 \quad (n \ge 5)\]
Kyun: \(6x - 6\) ka derivative 6 hai, jo constant hai. Constant ka derivative 0, aur 0 ka derivative phir 0. Is liye paanchwein se aage har derivative zero.
Dhyan dein: chauthe derivative se notation \(f^{(4)}\) bracket ke saath likhte hain, bina bracket ke \(f^{4}\) power samjhi jati hai.

Tasdeeq:
Degree 4 ke polynomial ka chautha derivative constant hota hai: \(4! \times \frac{1}{4} = 24 \times \frac{1}{4} = 6\). Yeh \(f^{(4)}(x) = 6\) se mil gaya.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Degree \(k\) wala polynomial \(k + 1\) dafa differentiate karne par zero ho jata hai. Is liye polynomial ke derivatives kahin na kahin ruk jate hain. Lekin \(e^{ax}\), \(\sin x\) ya \(\ln x\) jaise functions ke derivatives kabhi khatam nahi hote; wahan hum pattern dhoondte hain (Examples 13 aur 14).

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
\(y = x^{5}\) ke kitne derivatives zero se mukhtalif (non-zero) hain, aur \(y_{5}\) kya hai?
Jawab: paanch; \(y_{5} = 5! = 120\), aur \(y_{6} = 0\).

blocks.title: Example 12
blocks.problem: If \(x = e^{at}\) and \(y = e^{2at}\), show that \(x^{2}\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} - 2y = 0\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(x = e^{at}\) ...(1) aur \(y = e^{2at}\) ...(2), dono parameter \(t\) mein.
Saabit karna: \(x^{2}\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} - 2y = 0\).
Tareeqa: sab se pehle parametric differentiation (2.3.2) se \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) nikalenge. Phir usse sirf \(x\) aur \(y\) mein likhenge, taa ke usse dobara \(x\) ke lehaz se differentiate kar sakein (quotient rule). Aakhir mein jo aaye use diye hue result se milayenge.

(1) aur (2) ko \(t\) ke lehaz se differentiate karein
\[\dfrac{dx}{dt} = ae^{at}, \quad \dfrac{dy}{dt} = 2ae^{2at}\]
(1) aur (2) ki madad se:
\[\dfrac{dx}{dt} = ax, \quad \dfrac{dy}{dt} = 2ay\]
Kyun: \(\frac{d}{dt}e^{kt} = ke^{kt}\). Phir \(e^{at}\) ki jagah \(x\) aur \(e^{2at}\) ki jagah \(y\) wapas likh diya, taa ke \(t\) se jaldi jaan chhoote.

Chain rule lagayein
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dy/dt}{dx/dt} = \dfrac{2ay}{ax}\]
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2y}{x} \quad \text{...(3)}\]
Kyun: parametric form mein \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy}{dt} \div \frac{dx}{dt}\) hota hai. \(a\) upar neeche cancel ho gaya.

(3) ko \(x\) ke lehaz se differentiate karein
\[\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = 2\cdot\dfrac{x\frac{dy}{dx} - y\cdot 1}{x^{2}}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{y}{x}\) par quotient rule: (neeche wala) \(\times\) (upar wale ka derivative) minus (upar wala) \(\times\) (neeche wale ka derivative), sab ko neeche wale ke square se divide.
Dhyan dein: \(y\) khud \(x\) ka function hai, is liye \(y\) ka derivative \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) hai, 1 nahi. Yahi sab se aam ghalti hai.

Equation (3) istemal karein
\[= 2\cdot\dfrac{\frac{2y}{x}\cdot x - y}{x^{2}}\]
\[= 2\cdot\dfrac{2y - y}{x^{2}} = \dfrac{2y}{x^{2}}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) ki jagah (3) se \(\frac{2y}{x}\) rakha. \(x\) cancel hua, aur \(2y - y = y\) bacha.

Tarteeb dein
\[x^{2}\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = 2y\]
\[\Rightarrow x^{2}\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} - 2y = 0\]
Kyun: dono taraf \(x^{2}\) se multiply kiya, phir \(2y\) left par le aaye. Yahi saabit karna tha.

Tasdeeq:
Ek chhupi hui baat: \(y = e^{2at} = (e^{at})^{2} = x^{2}\). To seedha \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = 2\), aur \(x^{2}\cdot 2 - 2x^{2} = 0\). Result bilkul sahi hai.
blocks.answer: \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{2y}{x}\) aur \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = \frac{2y}{x^{2}}\), is liye \(x^{2}\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} - 2y = 0\). Saabit ho gaya.

blocks.title: Note on numbering
blocks.text: Kitab is unit mein "Example 12" ka number do dafa istemal karti hai: yahan 2.8 mein aur phir 2.9.2 (Critical Point) mein. Hum chhape hue numbers hi rakhte hain, taa ke aap kitab se asani se mila sakein.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Parametric curve mein \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\) hargiz \(\frac{d^{2}y/dt^{2}}{d^{2}x/dt^{2}}\) nahi hota. Do sahi raaste hain: ya to \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) ko sirf \(x\) aur \(y\) mein likh kar \(x\) ke lehaz se differentiate karein (jaise Example 12 mein), ya yeh formula lagayein:
\[\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = \dfrac{d}{dt}\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)\cdot\dfrac{dt}{dx}\]
Yani \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) ko \(t\) ke lehaz se differentiate karo, phir \(\frac{dx}{dt}\) se divide karo.

blocks.title: Example 13
blocks.problem: Find all higher-order derivatives of the function \(y = e^{ax}\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(y = e^{ax}\), jahan \(a\) constant hai.
Maloom karna: \(\frac{dy}{dx}, \frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}, \ldots\) aur \(\frac{d^{n}y}{dx^{n}}\) ka aam formula.
Tareeqa: chain rule \(\frac{d}{dx}e^{u} = e^{u}\frac{du}{dx}\). Har dafa differentiate karne par ek \(a\) aur multiply hota hai. Chand derivatives nikal kar pattern (tarteeb) pehchanenge.

Pehla derivative
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{ax}\cdot\dfrac{d}{dx}(ax)\]
\[= e^{ax}\cdot a = ae^{ax}\]
Kyun: chain rule mein \(u = ax\), aur \(\frac{du}{dx} = a\). \(e^{u}\) ka derivative \(e^{u}\) hi rehta hai, sirf andar wale ka derivative saath multiply hota hai.

Doosra derivative
\[\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = a(e^{ax}a) = a^{2}e^{ax}\]
Kyun: \(a\) constant multiplier hai, woh bahar hi rehta hai; \(e^{ax}\) ka derivative phir \(e^{ax}a\). (Kitab bracket ke andar \(a^{ax}\) chhaap deti hai, neeche dekhiye.)

Teesra aur chautha derivative
\[\dfrac{d^{3}y}{dx^{3}} = a^{2}(e^{ax}a) = a^{3}e^{ax}\]
\[\dfrac{d^{4}y}{dx^{4}} = a^{4}e^{ax}\]
Kyun: har dafa wohi qadam: \(a\) ki power ek barh jati hai.

Aam pattern
\[\dfrac{d^{n}y}{dx^{n}} = a^{n}e^{ax} \quad (n \ge 1)\]
\[= a^{n}y\]
Kyun: \(n\)wein derivative tak \(a\) theek \(n\) dafa multiply ho chuka hota hai, aur \(e^{ax}\) to \(y\) hi hai.

Tasdeeq:
\(a = 1\) lein to \(y = e^{x}\), jis ka har derivative \(e^{x}\) hai; formula bhi \(1^{n}e^{x} = e^{x}\) deta hai. Theek.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
\(y = e^{-x}\) ka \(y_{7}\) kya hoga? Aur \(y = e^{3x}\) ka \(y_{5}\)?
Jawab: pehle mein \(a = -1\), to \(y_{7} = (-1)^{7}e^{-x} = -e^{-x}\). Matlab odd number wale derivatives par minus aur even wale par plus. Doosre mein \(a = 3\), to \(y_{5} = 3^{5}e^{3x} = 243e^{3x}\).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Example 13 mein kitab \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = a(a^{ax}a) = a^{2}e^{ax}\) likhti hai. Bracket ke andar \(e^{ax}a\) hona chahiye, jo \(e^{ax}\) ka derivative hai: \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = a(e^{ax}a) = a^{2}e^{ax}\). Aakhri jawab \(a^{2}e^{ax}\) sahi hai, sirf beech ki line mein printing ki ghalti hai.

blocks.title: Example 14
steps:
Diya gaya: \(y = \ln\sqrt{\frac{2x - 3}{x + 1}}\).
Maloom karna: \(y_{4}\), yani chautha derivative.
Tareeqa: seedha differentiate karna bohat lamba hoga. Is liye pehle logarithm ke qawaneen (laws) se \(y\) ko do saada logs ke farq mein badlenge. Phir har term ko power ki shakal \((2x-3)^{-1}\), \((x+1)^{-1}\) mein likh kar power rule aur chain rule se chaar dafa differentiate karenge.

Logarithm ki properties lagayein
\[y = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln\left(\dfrac{2x - 3}{x + 1}\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\ln(2x-3) - \ln(x+1)\right]\]
Kyun: \(\sqrt{u} = u^{1/2}\) aur \(\ln u^{k} = k\ln u\), is liye \(\frac{1}{2}\) bahar aa gaya. Phir \(\ln\frac{p}{q} = \ln p - \ln q\).

Pehla derivative
\[y_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{2}{2x-3} - \dfrac{1}{x+1}\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\left(2(2x-3)^{-1} - (x+1)^{-1}\right)\]
Kyun: \(\frac{d}{dx}\ln u = \frac{1}{u}\frac{du}{dx}\). \(2x - 3\) ka andar wala derivative 2 hai, aur \(x + 1\) ka 1. Phir fractions ko negative power mein likha taa ke agla derivative aasaan ho.

Doosra derivative
\[y_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(-4(2x-3)^{-2} + (x+1)^{-2}\right)\]
Kyun: \(\frac{d}{dx}(2x-3)^{-1} = -1\cdot(2x-3)^{-2}\cdot 2\). Aage pehle se 2 tha, to \(2 \times (-1) \times 2 = -4\). Doosri term: \(-1 \times (-1) = +1\).
Dhyan dein: \(2x - 3\) ka andar wala 2 har qadam par dobara aata hai. Isi ko bhoolna sab se aam ghalti hai (aur kitab bhi yahi ghalti karti hai).

Teesra derivative
\[y_{3} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(16(2x-3)^{-3} - 2(x+1)^{-3}\right)\]
Kyun: \(-4 \times (-2) \times 2 = 16\), aur doosri term \(1 \times (-2) = -2\).

Chautha derivative
\[y_{4} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(-96(2x-3)^{-4} + 6(x+1)^{-4}\right)\]
\[y_{4} = \dfrac{-48}{(2x-3)^{4}} + \dfrac{3}{(x+1)^{4}}\]
Kyun: \(16 \times (-3) \times 2 = -96\) aur \(-2 \times (-3) = 6\); phir dono ko aadha kiya.

Kitab mein kya chhapa hai
Kitab \(y_{2}\) se aage \((2x-3)\) ka andar wala 2 chhor deti hai, is liye us ke \(y_{2}\), \(y_{3}\), \(y_{4}\) ghalat hain aur aakhri jawab \(\frac{-6}{(2x-3)^{4}} + \frac{3}{(x+1)^{4}}\) aata hai. Sahi lines upar wali hain (neeche "Kitab ki ghalti" dekhiye).

Tasdeeq:
\(y\) ka \((2x-3)\) wala hissa \(\frac{1}{2}\ln(2x-3)\) hai. Is ka \(n\)wan derivative \(\frac{1}{2}(-1)^{n-1}(n-1)!\,\frac{2^{n}}{(2x-3)^{n}}\) hai. \(n = 4\) par \(\frac{1}{2}\times(-1)\times 6\times 16 = -48\). Bilkul \(\frac{-48}{(2x-3)^{4}}\) se mil gaya.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
\(y = \ln(3x + 1)\) ka \(y_{2}\) nikaaliye.
Jawab: \(y_{1} = \frac{3}{3x+1} = 3(3x+1)^{-1}\), phir \(y_{2} = 3 \times (-1)(3x+1)^{-2} \times 3 = -\frac{9}{(3x+1)^{2}}\). Dekhiye 3 do dafa aaya: ek pehle derivative mein aur ek doosre mein. Yahi chain rule ka andar wala factor hai jo har qadam par saath aata hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Example 14 mein kitab \(y_{1}\) ke baad har qadam par chain rule ka factor 2 (\(2x - 3\) ka derivative) bhool jati hai. Woh \(y_{2} = \frac{1}{2}\left(-2(2x-3)^{-2} + (x+1)^{-2}\right)\), \(y_{3} = \frac{1}{2}\left(4(2x-3)^{-3} - 2(x+1)^{-3}\right)\) aur \(y_{4} = \frac{-6}{(2x-3)^{4}} + \frac{3}{(x+1)^{4}}\) likhti hai. Sahi: \(y_{2} = \frac{1}{2}\left(-4(2x-3)^{-2} + (x+1)^{-2}\right)\), \(y_{3} = \frac{1}{2}\left(16(2x-3)^{-3} - 2(x+1)^{-3}\right)\), aur \(y_{4} = \frac{-48}{(2x-3)^{4}} + \frac{3}{(x+1)^{4}}\). Exam mein sahi wala hi likhiye.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Pehle logarithm ke qawaneen kyun lagaye? Agar \(\ln\sqrt{\frac{2x-3}{x+1}}\) ko seedha differentiate karte to ek hi waqt mein chain rule, square root aur quotient rule teeno lagte, aur har agle derivative ke saath jawab aur ulajhta jata. Todne ke baad har term ek saada power ban gayi, jise baar baar differentiate karna aasaan hai. Yeh ek achhi aadat hai: pehle simplify, phir differentiate.

blocks.title: Challenge!
blocks.text: Example 14 mein \(y_{10}\) nikaaliye (kitab "example 16" likhti hai; neeche dekhiye).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Is unit ka Example 16 (2.9 mein, increasing function aur stationary point ke baare mein) higher derivatives ka example hai hi nahi, is liye "example 16 mein \(y_{10}\)" be-maani hai. Yeh box Example 14 ke saath chhapa hai, is liye ghaliban Example 14 (ya Example 13) muraad hai. Example 14 ke liye: \(y_{10} = -181440\left[\frac{1024}{(2x-3)^{10}} - \frac{1}{(x+1)^{10}}\right]\); Example 13 ke liye: \(y_{10} = a^{10}e^{ax}\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Das dafa differentiate kiye baghair \(y_{10}\) kaise nikla? \(y_{1}, \ldots, y_{4}\) mein pattern dekhiye: \(\frac{1}{2}\ln(2x-3)\) ke coefficients \(1, -2, 8, -48\) hain (\(\frac{1}{(2x-3)^{n}}\) ke saath), yani \(\frac{1}{2}(-1)^{n-1}(n-1)!\,2^{n}\). Sign har dafa badalta hai, factorial barhta hai, aur 2 ki power barhti hai. Is liye
\[y_{n} = \dfrac{(-1)^{n-1}(n-1)!}{2}\;\times\]
\[\left[\dfrac{2^{n}}{(2x-3)^{n}} - \dfrac{1}{(x+1)^{n}}\right]\]
\(n = 10\) par \(\frac{(-1)^{9}\,9!}{2} = -181440\) aur \(2^{10} = 1024\).

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
\(y = \sin x\) ke derivatives (yeh misaal hamari hai): \(y_{1} = \cos x\), \(y_{2} = -\sin x\), \(y_{3} = -\cos x\), \(y_{4} = \sin x\). Chautha derivative wapas \(\sin x\)! Yani har chaar qadam baad cycle dobara shuru hota hai. Is liye \(y_{10}\) wohi hai jo \(y_{2}\) hai: \(-\sin x\), kyunke \(10 = 4 \times 2 + 2\).
Yeh "chaar ka cycle" wala tareeqa Exercise 2.3 ke Question 6 mein bohat kaam aayega, jahan \(y_{10}\) aur \(y_{11}\) bina poora hisaab kiye likhne hain. Bas yeh dekhiye ke number ko 4 se divide karne par baqi (remainder) kya bachta hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Higher-order derivative: derivative ka dobara derivative; \(y_{2} = \frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = f''(x)\).
2. Degree \(k\) ke polynomial ke liye \(n > k\) par \(f^{(n)}(x) = 0\).
3. \(\frac{d^{n}}{dx^{n}}e^{ax} = a^{n}e^{ax}\).
4. Parametric equations mein \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) nikal kar use dobara \(x\) ke lehaz se differentiate karein; second derivatives ko aapas mein divide kabhi na karein.
5. Bohat dafa differentiate karna ho to pehle logs ko simplify karein, aur har qadam par chain rule ka andar wala factor saath rakhein.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Chain rule ka factor chhor dena: \(\frac{d}{dx}(2x-3)^{-1} = -2(2x-3)^{-2}\) hai, \(-(2x-3)^{-2}\) nahi (yahi ghalti kitab ke Example 14 mein hai).
2. \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\) ko \(\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^{2}\) samajh lena.
3. Implicit ya parametric sawal mein \(y\) ko constant samajh lena: \(\frac{d}{dx}(y) = \frac{dy}{dx}\) hota hai.
4. Chauthe derivative ko \(f^{4}(x)\) likhna; sahi \(f^{(4)}(x)\) hai.
